{{Short description|none}} {{Infobox football match | title = 1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Final | image = 1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final programme.jpg | image_size = 250 | event = [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] | team1association = [[File:Limerick colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 3-7 | team2 = [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] | team2association = [[File:Kilkenny colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 1-7 | details = | date = 1 September 1940 | stadium = [[Croke Park]] | city = [[Dublin]] | man_of_the_match1a = | referee = [[John Joe Callinan]] ([[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]]) | attendance = 49,260 | weather = | previous = [[1939 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1939]] | next = [[1941 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1941]] }} The '''1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final''' was a [[hurling]] match played at [[Croke Park]] on 1 September 1940 to determine the winners of the [[1940 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]], a tournament organised by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] for the champions of the three hurling [[provinces of Ireland]]. It was the 53rd All-Ireland final. The match was contested by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] of Leinster and [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] of Munster, with Limerick winning by 3–7 to 1–7.{{cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/sport/gaelic-games/cregan-says-it-s-limerick-s-time-to-stand-up-and-fight-1.1889646|title=Cregan says it’s Limerick’s ‘time to stand up’ and fight|publisher=Irish Times|date=7 August 2014|access-date=10 August 2015|first=Ian|last=O'Riordan}} The All-Ireland final between Limerick and Kilkenny was the fifth championship meeting between the two teams. Kilkenny, the [[1939 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|reigning champions]], were appearing in their eighth final in ten years and were hoping to win their 13th title. Limerick were lining out in their fifth final in eight years and were hoping to claim a 6th championship title. Limerick's All-Ireland victory was their first since [[1936 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|1936]]. The win put them in joint fourth position, alongside [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] on the all-time roll of honour. Kilkenny's All-Ireland defeat was their tenth in a final. It was the first of three defeats in All-Ireland final before their next victory. {{Clear}} ==Match== ===Details=== {{football box |date=1 September 1940

Only the third final ever at that stage where the losing team opened with a goal (1906 & 1915).
